t: #3887 Incremental Even-Weighted Cycle Queries — Weighted Union-Find with Parity
o: We add edges one by one, keeping the invariant that every cycle has even total weight. Weighted (parity) union-find stores, for each node, the parity of the path weight to its root. Adding an edge between different components creates no cycle, so it is always accepted. Adding an edge within one component closes exactly the fundamental cycle whose parity is w XOR parity(u) XOR parity(v); since fundamental cycles generate the whole cycle space, all cycles stay even iff this value is 0. Example 1 rejects the third edge because 1 XOR 0 XOR 0 XOR ... yields an odd cycle; Example 2 accepts it because the closed cycle has parity 1 XOR 1 XOR 0 = 0.
k: Parity DSU: each node stores the parity of its path weight to its DSU root; find() accumulates parities during path compression.
An intra-component edge (u,v,w) is safe iff w XOR p(u) XOR p(v) == 0; inter-component edges are always safe.
Fundamental cycles form a basis of the cycle space, so checking the single new fundamental cycle suffices.

a.i: Maintain a DSU where par[x] is the XOR of weights on the path from x to its parent. find returns (root, parity-to-root) with path compression. On each edge, compare root parities to decide acceptance and, when merging, set the new child's parity so the invariant holds.
s: Initialize parent[i] = i, par[i] = 0 for all nodes.
find(x): recursively find the root, compressing and XOR-ing parities so par[x] becomes the parity to the root.
For edge (u,v,w): compute (ru,pu) and (rv,pv). If ru == rv, accept iff (w ^ pu ^ pv) == 0. Otherwise merge (attach ru under rv with parity pu ^ pv ^ w) and accept.
a.t: O((n + E) α(n)) — near-linear DSU operations with path compression.

w: This is the canonical technique (same family as bipartiteness checking with DSU). Present it directly; a BFS/DFS re-check per edge would be O(E*n) and too slow. Pitfalls: getting the merge parity formula wrong (derive it by writing parity(u) = par[u] XOR parity-to-root and solving), and forgetting that cross-component edges are unconditionally accepted. Follow-ups: reject edges creating odd cycles but report which edges were rejected, or handle weight updates.
